translations: Aman's pen stopped at the edge of the character for "death," and the ink slowly spread across the bamboo slip, as if writing this tragic story into the river of time. The sea wind blew through the two of them, and the leaves on the shore swayed gently, as if bidding farewell to this conflict. Nezha's smile disappeared, replaced by a sense of heavy responsibility. Aman looked up and saw Nezha's eyes flashing with determination, and he couldn't help but think to himself, "This kid is really a brave and capable one."

Nezha nodded slightly. Aman didn't move closer, but instead wrote on the bamboo slip: "Patrolling the sea, Night Witch Li Gan came ashore to accuse Nezha, and died in the K'unlun circle." The old pen lingered at the edge of the character for "death" for a long time, and the ink slowly seeped out. Nezha looked down at the K'unlun circle in his hand and finally understood that the previous commotion wasn't just a child's play. The sea wind blew through the two of them again, and the shore was silent once more.

The people who were out fishing slowly retreated further away. The woman who had been arguing with Aman earlier scooped up her child and tucked them behind her, and she didn't even bother to pick up her bamboo basket. Nezha wanted to say that Li Gan had raised his steel spear first, but the words got stuck in his throat when he realized that sentence couldn't bring the person on the ground back to life. He washed the K'unlun circle clean with river water, washed it again, and it still shone brightly, but his hand felt heavier than before. Aman added "Li Gan moved first" to the previous line and then quickly wrote down the result of Li Gan falling to the ground. He whispered, "You have to record the cause and the result; if you leave out one detail, people in the future won't be able to understand." Nezha nodded, and for the first time, he didn't find Aman's fussiness annoying. The sound of the waves in the distance suddenly became more rhythmic, as if someone was knocking on the sea floor. Aman closed the bamboo slip and hugged it to his chest, saying, "This one might not be just a matter of taking turns and getting hit." Nezha put the K'unlun circle back on his wrist and looked out at the waves, saying, "Then let me explain myself."

The water hadn't receded yet, but the wind had changed. The waves suddenly parted to the left and right, and Dragon Prince Ao Bing stepped out of the waves onto the shore. He saw Li Gan lying on the ground and his face immediately darkened. "Who was responsible?" he asked, his voice not loud but loud enough to drown out the sound of the waves. Nezha put the K'unlun circle back on his wrist and took a step forward, saying, "I was. He moved first, and I didn't stop him." Ao Bing gripped his sword tightly, saying, "The people of the East Sea don't get to decide what's right or wrong." Nezha lifted his chin, saying, "And the people of Chen Tang Gate don't get to intimidate others." Their words hung in the air, and the waves crashed against their feet.

"The Dragon Palace collapsed three corridors, the coral lamps shattered seventeen, and the Turtle Chancellor is still stuck in the fountain, shouting for help." Ao Bing threw his cloak into the water, and it immediately turned into a floating ice path, saying, "Will you pay up?"
Nezha scratched his ear, saying, "I'll pay. I lent you the Heavenly Silk to spin into a rope for ten years to keep it from breaking."
Ao Bing sneered, and his sword flashed in the light, its tip biting into the air. "Then use your spine as collateral."

The sword light flashed, and the fishermen on the shore knew that this wasn't something that could be settled with just a few words. The old sailor shouted to the others to flip over the small boat that had run aground, and the boat's hull faced outwards to block the flying rocks. Nezha heard the sound of the boat scraping against the ground and moved to the side, creating a gap between Ao Bing and the crowd. He then deliberately tapped his shoulder with the K'unlun circle, saying, "If you want to use my spine as collateral, come at me, don't include other people's boats in your accounts."

Ao Bing saw through his intention and adjusted his sword tip to point out to sea, saying, "You know how to protect people, but you don't know how to stop." Nezha replied quickly, "If I had stopped, it would have been me lying on the ground." He glanced at the water and said in a softer voice, "But I didn't mean for him to die."

This was the first time he had spoken the second half of the sentence. Aman's hand holding the pen paused for a moment, not adding the phrase "without intention, there is no fault" because the facts couldn't be smoothed over with just a few words. Ao Bing didn't lower his sword either, saying, "He was on a mission to patrol the sea, and his life can't be exchanged for just one sentence of regret." Nezha transferred the K'unlun circle from his left hand to his right hand, saying, "So I'm standing here. Your account is with me, not with the people of Chen Tang Gate."

A wave cut through the space between the two of them, making the pebbles at Nezha's feet clatter loudly. Ao Bing stepped onto the ice path and pressed his sword tip down; Nezha let out the Heavenly Silk from his wrist, letting the red cloth spread out on the water's surface. Neither of them made the first move, and neither did Aman or the crowd get involved. The old sailor had just managed to get the last child into the flipped-over boat when the child poked their head out from the boat's hull and asked in a whisper, "Who will win?" The old sailor pushed the child's head back, saying, "First, you have to win over this stubborn head of yours."

Nezha heard this and smiled slightly. Ao Bing's sword flashed in the light, and the tip of the sword sliced through the water, creating a row of ice shards. Nezha didn't back down, and the K'unlun circle blocked the sword's tip from above, while the Heavenly Silk wrapped around Ao Bing's wrist. The first collision sent both of them stumbling back a step, and the words they had been using to explain themselves were pushed aside by the real fight.
